To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MRF models are viable models for face detection and synthesis, and that the performance of MRF models can be increased by training them using face-like images.

(1) the second-order MRF model is more effective in detecting human faces than the first-order MRF model; (2) adding face-like images to the data base of face images increases the performance of the trained MRF model for face detection; and (3) adding non-face images to the data set does not degrade the performance of the model.
MRFs are viable models for human faces, MRF-based face detection works well, and the second-order MRF model is better than the first-order model.
